Penrite Oil becomes Principal Partner of Melbourne across the AFL and AFLW programs for two years, the biggest commercial partnership in the club's 168-year history, and takes on the Walk to the 'G for FightMND.
deals.headline: Penrite fuels a Dees record.

article.standfirst: Melbourne has signed the biggest commercial partnership in its 168-year history, and it's with a Melbourne-born oil brand.
body: Penrite Oil will be Principal Partner of the Melbourne Football Club across both its AFL and AFLW programs for the next two years. The Penrite logo will sit in two spots on the Demons' 2027 playing guernseys, and the club calls it the biggest commercial partnership in its 168-year history. No fee was disclosed.

It's been a quick climb. Penrite only came on board ahead of the 2026 season, and one year in the family-owned business has backed itself to take the top spot on the jumper. The partnership also hands Penrite the Walk to the 'G, the march to the MCG for FightMND before the King's Birthday clash with Collingwood, one of the biggest days on the footy calendar.

Club CEO Dan Taylor summed up the fit: "Like us, Penrite is iconic and proudly Australian, born and raised in Melbourne, and dedicated to its community." Penrite CEO Toby Dymond pointed to the brand's Australian-made, family-owned story and its Melbourne roots.

Oil and lubricant brands usually spend their sponsorship money in motorsport. Penrite putting principal partner money into an AFL club is a bet that footy in Victoria reaches more of its customers than another livery on a race car. It's also a clean example of the trial-season model more mid-sized Australian brands are using: sign on at a lower level, see the return, then go big.
What to watch next: the 2027 guernsey reveal, how Penrite activates the Walk to the 'G, and whether other first-year partners around the league get the same push to step up.
article.close: One season to prove it, then the biggest partnership in Dees history.

Lufthansa extends its partnership with the German Football Association through 2031, adding the women's national team to the men's team it has backed since 2005.

Prediction market Novig signs marketing partnerships with seven NHL clubs: the Bruins, Sabres, Hurricanes, Stars, Devils, Islanders and Flyers, its first with NHL teams.

Nationwide renews its NWSL partnership on a multiyear term, staying exclusive official insurance partner, adding life insurance and continuing as presenting sponsor of the Lauren Holiday Impact Award.

Commonwealth Bank sponsored the Kooyong event from 2002 to 2004 (Commonwealth Bank International). It ran unsponsored in 2005, before AAMI.
Macron dresses tournament officials at the ATP Cup, Melbourne Summer Series and Adelaide International in 2021.
Ford was the Australian Open's major sponsor until 2001; Kia replaced it from the 2002 tournament.
Tennis Australia ends IBM's technology partnership with the Australian Open after more than two decades (web, IT, apps and the serve-speed display). Infosys took over from 2019.
Ralph Lauren signs a global, long-term deal as the Australian Open's official outfitter from AO 2021. It ran six years; BOSS takes over from AO 2027.

AccorHotels signs a three-year deal (2016 to 2018) as the Australian Open's first official accommodation partner, renewed in December 2018 for three more years. Marriott Bonvoy took hotels from AO 2022.
Wilson was the Australian Open's official ball from 2006 through AO 2018. Dunlop took over from 2019.
Lavazza became the Australian Open's official coffee at AO 2016, part of its deal with all four Grand Slams. It's listed through AO 2019.

Coopers signs a five-year deal as the Australian Open's official beer and cider partner from 2017, replacing Heineken. It's last listed for AO 2019; Stella Artois had beer for AO 2020, then Peroni from 2021.
Country Road supplied uniforms for AO support staff from the 2018 tournament and is listed through AO 2019. Ralph Lauren became official outfitter from 2021.
Barilla joined the Australian Open for AO 2018, a couple of months after signing Roger Federer, and is listed through AO 2019.
Blackmores was an Australian Open partner from 2015, listed through AO 2019.
CPA Australia was the Australian Open's official accounting and business partner, listed for AO 2017 to 2019.
The Walt Disney Company Australia was the Australian Open's family entertainment partner for AO 2018 only.
Chinese water brand Ganten signs a five-year deal as the Australian Open's official water from AO 2018, replacing Australian brand Frantelle.
Häagen-Dazs signs as the Australian Open's official ice cream and sorbet partner from AO 2017. It's listed through AO 2019.
Garnier returned to the Australian Open for AO 2019 only, after a long break from the tournament.
Global law firm K&L Gates was an Australian Open partner, listed for AO 2017 to 2019.
La Roche-Posay was named the Australian Open's official sunscreen partner in November 2018. Bondi Sands took suncare from December 2020.
Optus was the Australian Open's telecommunications partner from 2001, strengthened in 2005, and is listed through AO 2019.
Seven, the Australian Open's broadcaster since 1973, extends its rights for 2015 to 2019. Nine bought the 2019 rights early and took over, so Seven's last AO was 2018.
Toshiba takes over from Panasonic as the Australian Open's official TV supplier for AO 2013, and later supplied printers. It's listed through AO 2022.
Vegemite, back in Australian hands under Bega, signs to sponsor AO 2018 with branding on the ballkid uniforms. It returned for 2019.
Bookmaker William Hill was the Australian Open's official wagering partner, listed for AO 2017 and 2018.
DeRUCCI became the Australian Open's official home furniture and bedding partner in October 2018, listed through AO 2022.

Bondi Sands becomes the Official Sunscreen Partner of AO 2021 and the Summer Series, replacing La Roche-Posay. It was extended to 2027 in January 2024 but was last listed for AO 2025; MECCA Cosmetica is the official SPF from 2026.
Maui Jim was the Australian Open's official sunglass partner, listed for AO 2020 and 2021.
Pure Blonde Organic Cider was the Australian Open's official cider from November 2019, before Somersby took cider in 2023.
TradeMax Global Markets (TMGM) was the Australian Open's official online trading platform from AO 2021, listed through AO 2023.
Treasury Wine Estates was the Australian Open's official wine supplier from AO 2019 to 2022. Its Penfolds and Squealing Pig brands carried on as partners.
Uber and Uber Eats were the Australian Open's official rideshare and food delivery partners from AO 2019; 2022 was their fourth and last year.
Initial was the Australian Open's official hygiene partner for AO 2021 and 2022.
Santos was the Australian Open's official natural gas partner ahead of AO 2021. It was no longer a sponsor by AO 2022, after climate group pressure.
Grainshaker Australian Vodka signs a three-year deal as the Australian Open's official vodka for 2021 to 2023. Grey Goose took vodka from 2025.
Gordon's Gin was an Australian Open partner for AO 2022 and 2023. Diageo's Tanqueray followed for 2024.

deals.headline: Nike's on the ball.
deals.summary: Nike becomes official match ball provider for every UEFA men's club competition, Champions League, Europa League and Conference League included, for four seasons from 2027-28 to 2031.

article.standfirst: From 2027, one ball will roll through every UEFA men's club competition, and it will carry a swoosh.
body: UC3, the commercial arm behind UEFA's club competitions, has named Nike the official match ball provider for the Champions League, Europa League and Conference League, along with the Super Cup, Youth League and Futsal Champions League. The partnership runs for four seasons, from 2027-28 through to 2031. No fee was disclosed by either side.

The headline detail is the bundling. It will be the first time all three major UEFA men's club competitions share a single ball provider, so a set of separate supplier slots becomes one platform. Nike Football's Vice President and General Manager Camilo Andrade put it plainly: "This is a long-term commitment for Nike." UC3 Co-Managing Director Guy-Laurent Epstein called Nike the official match ball provider for UEFA men's club competitions from 2027.

Why does a ball matter this much? It is the one piece of kit that is in shot for every minute of every match, from a cold early-round night in the Conference League to the Champions League final. Official balls are also products in their own right, sold to fans and clubs, which gives Nike a steady run of launch moments across every season.

For the category, it is a reminder that the big sportswear brands still see real value in the rights that sit underneath the game as well as in clubs and athletes. A competition-wide ball partnership reaches every team in every round, whoever wins.

What to watch next: the first Nike ball reveal ahead of 2027-28, how Nike handles a separate design for the final, and whether the women's club competitions follow the men's into a single-supplier model.
article.close: From 2027, every European club night kicks off with a Nike product in play.

deals.headline: ARN books five summers.
deals.summary: ARN signs a five-year partnership with Tennis Australia from AO27 as the Australian Open's audio partner and broadcaster, with live shows from Melbourne Park, a dedicated AO DAB+ channel in Sydney and Melbourne, iHeart streaming and an Are Media extension into ELLE and Gourmet Traveller.

article.standfirst: ARN has locked in the Australian Open for the next five years.
body: ARN and Tennis Australia have signed a five-year partnership that starts with AO27, announced at ARN's Upfront27 event this week. ARN's metro talent will broadcast live from Melbourne Park across the tournament, and the package goes well past the shows themselves: a dedicated Australian Open DAB+ channel in Sydney and Melbourne, live streaming on iHeart, podcasts, YouTube and social content, regional network coverage, and an Are Media extension that brings ELLE and Gourmet Traveller into the mix for advertisers. Neither side has put a number on it.

This isn't ARN's first summer at Melbourne Park. It was the AO's official audio partner in 2025, and this new term pushes the relationship out a long way further. ARN's chief content officer, Kerri Elstub, didn't undersell it: "This is a huge commitment and a major step up from where we've been."

The interesting bit is the shape. Audio partners used to mean a few live crosses and some branded promos. This reads more like ARN treating the AO as a three-week content tentpole: on-air, on a channel of its own, on streaming and in magazines, all pointed at one event every January. For a radio network trying to sell advertisers a summer story, owning that much of the biggest event on the calendar is the pitch.

For Tennis Australia it's another long-term partner, and one that reaches fans in the car, at work and on the train, not just in front of a screen. Five years also gives both sides time to build the AO channel into something listeners actually seek out rather than a one-summer experiment.
What to watch: what actually runs on the AO DAB+ channel in January, how ARN sells the Are Media add-on to brands, and whether other big Australian events start packaging audio rights the same way.
article.close: The AO's summer soundtrack is sorted for the next five Januarys.

deals.headline: Quest moves to the front.
deals.summary: Quest Apartment Hotels signs a three-year extension to become the Sharks' front-of-jersey major partner for the NRL side from 2027, while staying on with the NRLW team.

article.standfirst: Quest Apartment Hotels started on the Sharks' NRLW jersey. From 2027 it's on the front of the men's one too.
body: Quest Apartment Hotels has signed a three-year extension with the Cronulla Sharks that makes it the club's front-of-jersey major partner for the NRL side from the 2027 season. The club calls it a Premier Major Partner role. Quest isn't walking away from the women either: it stays on with the NRLW team, so the brand will sit on both Sharks jerseys.

The relationship isn't new. Quest came on board in 2024, backing the club's membership program and the NRLW side. Two years on, it has stepped up to the front of the men's jersey. David Mansfield, Managing Director of The Ascott Limited, Australasia, put it this way: "We're particularly proud to build on our support of the Sharks' women's team and now stand alongside both the men's and women's teams as a major partner."

That path is the bit worth noting. Women's sport keeps pitching itself to brands as a smart entry point: get in early, build the relationship, prove the fit. Quest is a working example of how that can play out in rugby league. It backed the NRLW team and the members first, then moved up to the main jersey with the same club, rather than arriving cold with a one-off front-of-jersey cheque.

It's a tidy fit on paper too. An accommodation brand gets a natural story with a club whose teams and travelling fans are on the road most weekends, and members who already know the name from the membership program. The Sharks get a partner that has already shown it will put money into more than one part of the club.

What to watch: how Quest uses the jersey in 2027, whether the NRLW and NRL assets are sold together in its activation, and whether other NRL clubs start pointing brands at the women's jersey as the way in.
article.close: The NRLW partnership was the audition. Quest got the part.

deals.headline: Dressed for the walk in.
deals.summary: Menswear chain CONNOR signs a two-year partnership to dress Sydney FC's first team, coaches and officials for matchday arrivals and club functions.

article.standfirst: Sydney FC has sold the walk from the team bus to the sheds.
body: CONNOR has signed a two-year partnership with Sydney FC as the club's Official Off-Field Style Partner. The Australian menswear chain will supply suiting and fashion outfits for the first team, coaching staff and club officials, covering matchday arrivals and club functions. The partnership also takes in matchday activations, player appearances, in-store experiences and offers for members.

The split in the wardrobe is the interesting part. Under Armour stays as the club's on-field apparel partner, so CONNOR is buying a different moment: what the players wear before and after the whistle. Football clubs have long had a formalwear line in the commercial deck, but the arrival has become a piece of content in its own right, and that gives a tailored-clothing brand something it can actually use.

The fit between brand and fans is the pitch. CONNOR has more than 200 stores across Australia and New Zealand, and its general manager, Marc Miller, described its customer as someone who is at the game on the weekend and following his team all season. Matt Pound, Sydney FC General Manager Commercial and Marketing, made the same point from the club's side: "Importantly, this partnership goes beyond outfitting the team."

For a mid-market retailer, that is a neat piece of category thinking. A store network means the partnership has somewhere to land beyond a logo on a backdrop, and player appearances give the shops a reason to shout about it. Sydney FC's commercial team, meanwhile, gets a new line item that doesn't tread on its kit partner.

The thing to watch is how much of this turns up where fans actually see it. If the arrivals become regular content and the in-store offers feel like more than a discount code, expect other A-League clubs to go looking for their own off-field partner.
article.close: The kit partnership gets the logo. This one gets the arrival shot.

deals.headline: Milan's new home gets a name.
deals.summary: Generali takes naming rights to the 71,500-seat stadium AC Milan and Inter plan for 2031/32, and becomes Official Insurance Partner of both clubs.

article.standfirst: San Siro's replacement has a name already, and it reportedly cost Generali about €650m.
body: AC Milan and Inter have unveiled the Generali Stadium, the 71,500-seat ground they plan to share in Milan, with the Italian insurer taking the naming rights and becoming Official Insurance Partner of both clubs. The clubs call it one of the largest stadium naming rights agreements in global sport. They haven't disclosed the terms.

The reported number is about €650m, carried by ESPN, Sportcal and Il Sole 24 Ore among others. The length is less settled. Most reports say 20 years, which works out at about €32.5m a year, while Il Sole 24 Ore says 25. Treat both as reported, not confirmed.

The timing is the interesting part. Construction isn't expected to start until 2028, and the first match is targeted for the 2031/32 season, subject to approvals. So Generali has put its name on a building that exists as a set of renders, around five years before anyone sits in it.

That's a different shape to most naming rights partnerships, where a brand buys into a venue fans can already see. Here the insurer gets in at the start, and the name is on the project from day one rather than arriving later to sit awkwardly beside an old one. Nobody will have to be talked out of calling the new place something else.

It also buys two fan bases at once. Most stadium names sit with one club and one set of supporters. This one covers both sides of one of the biggest rivalries in Europe, in the insurer's home market. The Official Insurance Partner role gives it a commercial reason to be in front of both clubs well before the building opens.

What to watch next is the approvals, because the 2031/32 target depends on them, and the partner line-up that follows. A name this size sets the tone for everything else the clubs try to sell around the building, and a shared stadium gives every other category the same two-for-one pitch.
article.close: Two rivals, one name on the door, and the first game still about five years off.

deals.headline: Maccas joins the Warriors.
deals.summary: McDonald's NZ joins the One NZ Warriors as restaurant partner on a three-year partnership, with the golden arches on the shorts of all six Warriors teams.

article.standfirst: McDonald's has joined the One NZ Warriors on a three-year partnership, and the golden arches are going on the shorts.
body: McDonald's New Zealand has become the One NZ Warriors' restaurant partner on a three-year partnership announced on 1 November. The money wasn't disclosed. The golden arches will sit on the left back of the shorts for all six Warriors teams: the NRL and NRLW sides, plus the NSW Cup, Jersey Flegg Cup, SG Ball Cup and Harold Matthews Cup squads.

That reach through the pathway grades is the detail worth noticing. A lot of club partnerships live on the top-grade jersey and nowhere else. This one puts the brand on every team the club fields, from the juniors up to the NRL squad.

The timing suits McDonald's. The announcement lines up with 50 years since its first New Zealand restaurant opened in Porirua in 1976. The company says it now runs almost 180 outlets across the country, with more than 90 per cent of them owned by franchisees. A club with a national following and a young supporter base is a natural place to mark a milestone like that.

On the club side, the restaurant category has had a long-serving name in it. Wendy's has been a Warriors partner since 2008 and is described in the club's release as the outgoing partner. The club's CEO Cameron George thanked Wendy's for almost 20 years of support. Neither release says McDonald's takes over from Wendy's, so we won't either.

What to watch next is how the arches show up in the club's marketing once the new season gets closer, and whether the pathway teams get the same activation as the NRL side. The Warriors have kept adding commercial partners this year, and a brand this size in the quick-service category gives the club another big name to build around.
article.close: Same arches, every grade, three years.

deals.summary: OXEN becomes the Dolphins' on-field apparel partner from 2027, with the ECHO home jersey unveiled alongside.

article.standfirst: A UK sportswear brand has landed one of the NRL's newest clubs, and the Dolphins will play in OXEN from 2027.
body: The Dolphins have named OXEN as their On-Field Apparel Partner from 2027. The club's own announcement also calls the brand its Official Technical and Kit Partner, and the partnership covers supporter merchandise as well as the playing kit. No length or value has been disclosed.

OXEN is a UK-founded performance sportswear and lifestyle brand, and it already knows the club. It has already backed the Dolphins Academy and been a boot partner for the club, so this is a step up from the Academy and the boots to the main jersey. The new ECHO home jersey was unveiled alongside the announcement.

The club's chief executive Terry Reader said OXEN has been a valued partner and the club is keen to take the relationship to the next level. OXEN Sports chief executive Lee Jenkinson said the brand was proud to be joining the Dolphins at such an exciting stage in the club's journey.

OXEN has also been building a local footprint. The announcement says the company has invested in an Australian headquarters and distribution centre, which matters when you are supplying a club's merchandise as well as its match kit. It is also already in the NRL ecosystem as the Parramatta Eels' footwear partner, a partnership announced in 2025.

Why it matters: a challenger brand is taking on a whole NRL club, playing kit and supporter range included, rather than just boots. For the Dolphins it means a supplier that is already invested locally and that has plenty to prove, and for OXEN it puts its product in front of a full NRL crowd.
Watch for how OXEN uses the partnership at retail and how the ECHO jersey sells.
article.close: OXEN has moved from the boots to the jersey, and the Dolphins are the test case.

deals.summary: adidas became the Storm's Official Apparel Partner in a multi-year partnership covering kit for the NRL squad, pathways and academy, with the new jersey debuting in Las Vegas.

article.standfirst: adidas is the Melbourne Storm's new Official Apparel Partner, and the three stripes will make their debut in Las Vegas.
body: Melbourne Storm have named adidas as their Official Apparel Partner on a multi-year agreement. The partnership runs through adidas Pacific and covers playing kit, training, performance and lifestyle apparel for the NRL squad, the club's elite male and female pathway teams and its academy programs. Neither side has put a number on it or said how long it lasts.

The timing does a lot of the work. The Storm's new jersey is set to debut when the club opens its 2027 season in Las Vegas, a first for the club on US soil. Storm executive Tayah Bot says the club will be debuting the new jersey on the world stage. For a global sportswear brand, that is a made-for-TV launch moment with an American audience watching an NRL strip for the first time.

It also shows how far the apparel conversation has moved. A kit partnership used to be about the jersey and the merch rack. This one spans the pathways, the women's program and the academy, which means one brand shapes how the club looks from junior representative level up. adidas Pacific's Rachel Howard is on the record backing the club's elite programs, which tells you where the brand sees the value.

For the NRL, it is another sign that the big global sportswear names see rugby league as worth a serious play, particularly when the schedule gives them a stage like Vegas. For rivals, it raises the bar on what an apparel partner is expected to bring beyond supplying kit.
What to watch next: the jersey reveal itself, how adidas uses the Vegas trip in its global marketing, and whether the retail range lands before or after the big night.
article.close: The Storm have picked their moment. Vegas is the runway.

article.standfirst: Youi has signed on as an official partner of the men's and women's Big Bash leagues, and it is backing five clubs on top.
body: Youi has become an official partner of Cricket Australia's two Big Bash competitions, the KFC BBL and the Weber WBBL. The insurer is also signing direct partnerships with five clubs: Brisbane Heat, Hobart Hurricanes, Melbourne Renegades, Melbourne Stars and Sydney Thunder. The club releases went out on Monday 26 October, with trade coverage following a day later. Length and value were not disclosed.

The visible parts are easy to spot. Youi will be on the playing kit of those five clubs through the BBL|16 season, and on umpire uniforms in both the men's and women's competitions. The partnership kicks off with the opening of WBBL|12 on Thursday 29 October, so the brand gets its first look at a live audience within days of the announcement.

What stands out is the shape of it. One brand holds a league-wide partner role and also sits on the shirts of five of the competition's clubs. Most insurers pick one or the other. Splitting the spend across the league and a majority of its clubs gives Youi both the broadcast-level exposure and the local, club-level relationships that tend to build loyalty.

Youi is also leaning on the fans rather than the players. Its marketing chief, Angela Greenwood, says the brand wants to celebrate fans, communities and volunteers, and the plan includes match-day fan engagement, volunteer recognition and grassroots community cricket activations. In a category where insurers fight for attention, a pitch built around the people in the stands and the local clubs is a sensible fit for a summer competition that runs through the holidays.

For the Big Bash, it adds another name to a sponsor list that already carries plenty of big brands. For rival insurers, it raises the bar on how much of the cricket calendar one competitor can own. Watch how Youi uses the five-club structure, and whether the league-wide rights lead to more in-stadium activity once the men's season starts.
article.close: One insurer, two leagues, five clubs. That is a serious summer.

deals.headline: NBA lets markets in.
deals.summary: The NBA named Kalshi and Polymarket its preferred prediction market exchanges, with IP rights, official Sportradar data and a CFTC information-sharing agreement alongside.

article.standfirst: The NBA has named Kalshi and Polymarket its preferred prediction market exchanges, and a regulator agreement came with them.
body: The NBA announced on Monday, US time, that Kalshi and Polymarket are now its preferred prediction market exchanges. Both get the right to use NBA intellectual property, including league and team names and logos, plus marketing and promotional rights across the United States. How long the arrangements run and what the exchanges are paying haven't been disclosed.

The data and the rules are as important as the branding. Both exchanges will settle authorised markets using official NBA data from Sportradar, the league's official data distribution partner. In return the NBA has laid down conditions: players, league employees and team employees can't trade on NBA contracts, the range of markets is limited, and information on suspicious trading gets shared. The sportsbook restrictions the league set earlier this month, such as the ban on parlays built on unders for low-minute players, will apply to prediction markets as well.

A regulator is part of the picture too. The NBA signed a memorandum of understanding with the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission to share information and build a framework for NBA-related markets. The Block reports the NBA is the third league to sign one, after MLB and the NHL. DraftKings, already an NBA marketing partner, has widened its partnership to cover prediction markets nationwide and carries the status of authorised prediction market operator.

For sponsorship, the interesting part is the order of operations. Prediction markets have lived in a grey zone, and the league has put guardrails and a regulator's paperwork around them before putting the logos out. That gives other rights holders a template and gives the exchanges a sanctioned place in a sport that fills its arenas and its feeds. It also sets up the next fight over who else gets in.

Watch for the follow-ups. The league has said it will add more partners in the coming weeks, and Front Office Sports reports Novig is expected to sign later this week. The WNBA isn't automatically covered, so the exchanges would need separate partnerships for that. And the NFL is the major US league still without a commercial partnership with prediction markets.
article.close: The league has signed up for the money and the guardrails at the same time.

deals.headline: US money lands at Mestalla.

article.standfirst: Valencia has sold 42% of the club to a US consortium with KKR's co-founders and the Denver Broncos' owners among its backers.
body: Pitchwise Holdings has agreed to buy a 42% stake in Valencia CF from Meriton Holdings, the company Peter Lim has used to own the club. The partnership was announced on Friday 23 October. It values Valencia at €1.25 billion including debt, and investors will also put €100 million of new capital into the club. Meriton keeps majority control and Kiat Lim stays on as president.

Pitchwise is a consortium of family offices and long-term institutional investors, led by Ann Rodriguez and Corey Woolfolk, who join Lim in the new ownership group. The backers are the headline: KKR co-founders George Roberts and Henry Kravis, plus Penner Sports Group, the Denver investment business whose portfolio includes the NFL's Broncos.

Read the €1.25 billion carefully. It is an enterprise value, debt included, so it doesn't mean the 42% cost €525 million. The split between the share purchase and the €100 million injection hasn't been disclosed, so neither will we guess it.

What Valencia sold was a story about the future. The club says the valuation reflects its men's and women's teams, the 49,000-seat Mestalla and the Nou Mestalla project, planned to hold more than 70,000. That is a minority stake priced on a stadium that hasn't opened, and US money keeps showing it will pay for exactly that kind of upside in European football.

What to watch: regulatory approval and the other closing conditions, how quickly the new capital shows up at Nou Mestalla, and whether the new owners bring the American playbook with them, from naming rights to premium seating, once the stadium is built.
article.close: Valencia's new partners are betting on what Mestalla becomes.

article.standfirst: Visa has bought its way into the Kentucky Derby.
body: Churchill Downs has named Visa the Preferred Payment Partner of the racetrack and the 153rd Kentucky Derby, announced on Tuesday 20 October US time. The track's own release calls it a first-of-its-kind, multi-year partnership. It doesn't say how many years, and it doesn't put a dollar figure on it, so neither will we.

The pitch is about the punter at the gate. Visa clients and cardholders get exclusive Derby Weekend offers, experiences and better ways to buy. Churchill Downs says the partnership should make ticket purchases more efficient and accessible. That is a payments company talking about the checkout, not just a logo on a rail.

Visa joins the track's existing Signature Partners, which the release lists as Woodford Reserve, Longines, Ford and SAP. That is a tight club: a bourbon, a watch brand, a carmaker and a software giant. Slotting a payments brand in alongside them says the Derby now sees the transaction itself as something worth selling.

The timing is clear too. The 153rd Derby runs on Saturday 1 May 2027, and the race carries a $5 million purse. Visa gets about six months to build activation before the roses are even on the shelf. Australians will know the company from its Rugby World Cup tie-up, so racing is another big, crowd-heavy property for it.

What to watch: whether the Derby Weekend offers reach cardholders outside the US, whether Churchill Downs adds more payments or ticketing partners around the tracks it runs, and what Visa builds for ticket buyers before May.
article.close: The Derby just got a new way to take your money.

article.standfirst: Hahn has landed the biggest pour of the Australian summer.
body: Tennis Australia has named Lion's Hahn the Official Beer of the Australian Open and the Australian Summer of Tennis in a multi-year partnership announced on Thursday 22 October. Neither side has put a length or a number on it, so we won't either.

It's a changing of the guard in the beer category. Asahi Beverages has held it since 2021, when Peroni became the AO's Official Beer, and Peroni and Balter were still pouring at Melbourne Park in January. From AO27 it's Lion's turn, with Hahn front and centre.

The centrepiece is Hahn House, a two-storey venue with a beer garden on Grand Slam Oval, which Tennis Australia is pitching as a new social hub for the tournament. Lion is bringing more of its portfolio too: Stone & Wood takes over Garden Square, and Four Pillars runs a new gin bar at Kia Arena.

Away from Melbourne Park, Hahn plans limited-edition packaging, competitions, tennis merch and surprise experiences, plus pop-up pickleball courts and racket-shaped drinks trays around the country. That reach matters. The AO is a fortnight, but the Summer of Tennis gives Hahn a whole season of pub and bottle-shop activity to hang it on.

It also rounds out a big sporting slate for the brand. Hahn already holds the naming rights to the Hahn Australia Cup and is the official beer of the Wallabies, so the AO gives Lion a marquee summer property to sit alongside its football and rugby plays.
What to watch: how Hahn House lands with AO crowds in January, and whether Lion stacks more of its brands across the Summer of Tennis events outside Melbourne.
article.close: Summer's sorted: the AO has picked its beer.

article.standfirst: Woolworths has put its hand up for both home Rugby World Cups.
body: Woolworths has been named the Official Supermarket Supporter of the men's Rugby World Cup 2027 and the women's Rugby World Cup 2029, both being played in Australia. The partnership was announced on Tuesday 20 October. Neither side has put a number or an end date on it beyond the two tournaments, so we won't either.

It slots Woolworths into World Rugby's Official Suppliers and Supporters tier, alongside names like Dove Men+Care, Gilbert, Macron and Mitsubishi Estate. Above that sit the official partners (Liqui Moly, Coca-Cola, IHG) and the principal partners, Emirates, Asahi Super Dry and Visa.

The interesting bit is the retail media angle. Woolworths says its Cartology network will open up brand opportunities around the tournaments. That turns a supermarket sponsorship into something bigger: a channel other brands can buy into, with the World Cup as the hook and the checkout as the payoff. Woolworths reckons it serves around 24 million customers a week, which is a lot of eyeballs for a pack of snags or a slab of something cold.

The men's tournament runs from 1 October to 13 November 2027, with 24 teams across seven host cities. Woolworths is pitching itself as a one-stop shop for fans on both sides of the Tasman, with fans in New Zealand part of the pitch as much as fans here.
What to watch: how hard Woolworths pushes Cartology partnerships off the back of this, and whether the other big grocers or liquor chains try to muscle in around the edges with their own rugby plays.
article.close: In a home World Cup, the supermarket aisle might be the best seat in the house.

deals.headline: IREN lands at the Bernabéu.
deals.summary: Sydney-founded AI cloud provider IREN is Real Madrid's new official sponsor, reported as the club's official AI cloud partner.

article.standfirst: A Sydney-founded AI cloud company has just put its name next to the biggest badge in club football.
body: Real Madrid named IREN as a new official sponsor on Sunday 18 October. Trade coverage from Sportcal and Footy Headlines has IREN billed as the club's official AI cloud partner. Neither side has said how long the partnership runs or what it's worth, so we won't guess.

If the name rings a bell, it should. IREN started out in Sydney, is listed on the Nasdaq and now runs as an AI cloud and data centre business. In June it signed a multi-year partnership to put its badge on Golden State Warriors jerseys from the 2026-27 season, a patch reportedly worth more than US$50 million a year and reportedly the richest sponsorship in North American team sport.

The Madrid partnership makes more sense once you look at where IREN is building. In June it completed the purchase of Spanish data centre developer Nostrum Group, picking up around 490 megawatts of secured power in Spain. So this isn't just a logo on a stadium screen. IREN is buying awareness in a country where it's putting real infrastructure in the ground, and doing it with the one club everyone in Spain, and most of the planet, knows.

For the category, this is the AI infrastructure money finally reaching European football's top table. Crypto and fintech brands bought their way into sport on hype. The compute crowd has hard assets, big customers and a reason to be known by governments, landlords and talent as much as by fans. Expect them to keep paying for the biggest badges they can find.

What to watch: whether IREN's role grows into matchday branding or technology work at the Bernabéu, and whether the Warriors and Real Madrid become a template for more AI cloud firms chasing global clubs.
article.close: AI cloud money has found the biggest stage in club football, and it won't be the last.

deals.headline: GWM rolls into Parra.
deals.summary: Multi-year partnership makes GWM the Eels' official automotive partner from 2027, with its logo on the sleeve of both the NRL and NRLW playing jerseys.

article.standfirst: GWM wants to be Australia's number five car brand, and it's driving through Parramatta to get there.
body: The Parramatta Eels have signed GWM as their official automotive partner on a multi-year partnership that kicks off in the 2027 season. The car maker also takes the sleeve on both the NRL and NRLW playing jerseys, so the same badge runs across the men's and women's programs. Neither side has put a number on it.

It's been a big week in the Eels' commercial office. Two days earlier the club confirmed adidas as its new apparel partner across the NRL and NRLW sides, with the new kit due in Round 1 next year. So by the time Parra runs out in 2027 the jersey, and what's printed on the arm, will both be new.

For GWM this is part of a pattern. It's already the official automotive partner of the NZ Warriors and a joint major partner at Richmond in the AFL. GWM's Australia and New Zealand chief operating officer John Kett was blunt about the goal: become the country's number five automotive brand. He also had a crack at the club's ambitions, saying that for Parramatta the goal is premiership number five.

The logic is easy to follow. New South Wales is the biggest car market in the country and western Sydney is a heartland of rugby league, so a sleeve at Parra puts the brand in front of a huge chunk of potential buyers every week. Taking the asset across both the NRL and NRLW kits also squeezes more airtime out of one spot on the shirt, and gives GWM a presence in the women's game without a separate partnership.

What to watch next: how GWM activates it. Car brands in footy usually lean on vehicle fleets, member offers and dealer tie-ins, so expect GWM to show up well beyond the sleeve. The other thing to watch is whether GWM keeps adding clubs. Two codes and three big teams in, it's starting to look like a portfolio rather than a one-off.
article.close: New kit, new car partner, same week. Not a bad start to 2027 for the Eels.

deals.summary: Multi-year partnership makes adidas the Eels' official apparel partner across the NRL and NRLW teams, academy and junior rep sides, with the new kit debuting in Round 1 2027.

article.standfirst: adidas is putting the Parramatta Eels in three stripes.
body: The Parramatta Eels have signed a multi-year partnership that makes adidas the club's official apparel partner. It covers a lot of ground: the NRL and NRLW teams, the club's elite academy programs and its junior representative sides. Both top teams will run out in adidas for the first time in Round 1 of the 2027 season. Neither side has put out a length or a dollar figure.

The club launched it with a campaign called "Made for Parra", and the kit and retail range are due to be unveiled at a launch later this year. That reveal is where the fans get their first proper look at what three stripes in blue and gold actually means.

Why it matters: apparel is one of the few partnerships that touches every part of a club. Sponsors get a logo on a jersey. A kit supplier gets the jersey itself, the training gear, the merch store and every junior player pulling on a Parra top on a Saturday morning. Signing the pathways as well as first grade means adidas is in front of the next generation of Eels fans years before they buy a membership.

It's also a nice get for adidas, a brand most Aussie fans link with football and rugby union rather than the NRL. Landing the Eels in Western Sydney, with a partnership that runs right down to the juniors, gives it a real foothold in rugby league heartland.
What to watch next: the kit reveal and how hard adidas pushes the retail side, and whether the brand follows up with more rugby league clubs once the Eels range is on the shelves.
article.close: When a global brand dresses the juniors too, it's buying the next generation of fans.

deals.headline: Monaco's shirt for Europe.
deals.summary: Monaco insurance broker takes the front of the shirt for AS Monaco's Conference League games this season, plus LED boards at Stade Louis-II.

article.standfirst: Monaco has signed a shirt sponsor just for its European nights.
body: AS Monaco has named Suisscourtage Assurances its new major partner for the UEFA Conference League. The insurance broker's name goes on the front of the first-team shirt for European matches this season, and it picks up LED advertising at home games at Stade Louis-II. No fee or length beyond the coming season has been put out. The campaign starts away to CSKA Sofia on Thursday 15 October.

It's a local partnership through and through. Suisscourtage was founded in Monaco in 1988, sits inside the JV Pastor Group and employs 220 people, working with private clients and businesses that need cover for complex risks and high-value assets. Monaco CEO Thiago Scuro pitched it as two Monegasque organisations joining forces, and that's the point: a club from a tiny principality putting a home-grown business on the shirt when it travels.

The timing tells the story. Only last week Monaco signed Mammouth AI as a premium partner through 2029, with the AI company appearing on the shirt in Ligue 1. This is Monaco's first go at the Conference League, so rather than bundle Europe into an existing partnership, the club treated it as fresh inventory and sold it separately.

That's the bit worth watching across the game. Competition-specific shirt partnerships let clubs squeeze more out of the same piece of fabric, and they open the door to brands that can't stretch to a full-season domestic partnership but can afford a European run. For a broker chasing wealthy clients, a handful of televised European nights with a club tied to Monaco is a tidy fit.

What to watch next: how far Monaco go in the competition, because a deeper run means more matches and more value for Suisscourtage, and whether the partnership rolls over if Monaco land back in the Champions League.
article.close: Expect more clubs to sell the shirt one competition at a time.

deals.headline: Adobe serves up AI.
deals.summary: Multi-year partnership as Official AI Marketing and Creativity Partner. Adobe's first tennis sponsorship worldwide.

article.standfirst: Adobe just signed its first tennis sponsorship anywhere in the world, and it picked the Australian Open.
body: Tennis Australia has named Adobe the Official AI Marketing and Creativity Partner of the Australian Open in a multi-year partnership that will roll out in phases. Neither side has put a number or an end date on it. What they have spelled out is the job: Tennis Australia will run Adobe CX Enterprise across its digital setup to get a sharper read on what fans actually want, then use that to steer them to the right match, somewhere to eat or a bit of entertainment at Melbourne Park, and to tailor its comms market by market.

It's a big first for Adobe. The software giant has never backed tennis before, so the AO becomes its entry point into the sport globally. That's a handy feather in Tennis Australia's cap, which keeps pitching the AO as the Grand Slam of Asia-Pacific and wants partners who can help it reach that regional audience.

The interesting bit is how the value flows. Plenty of tech partnerships in sport stop at a logo on the court and a line in the release. This one only works if the product is actually used, and used well. Tennis Australia gets enterprise tools to personalise at a scale it couldn't build itself, and Adobe gets a two-week global shop window every January to show its AI doing something useful for real people. Fans also get AI creative tools to make their own content, which ticks the engagement box and feeds more first-party data back into the system.

The brief runs well past the tournament too. Both sides say the aim is year-round participation across Australia and the wider Asia-Pacific, which puts the partnership squarely in the business of growing the game for the other fifty weeks of the year.

What to watch: how much of this fans actually notice at AO 2027. If the personalisation lands and the creative tools get used, expect other rights holders to start writing data and martech into their partner briefs rather than just selling space.
article.close: The AO has long called itself the Grand Slam of Asia-Pacific. Now it's got the martech to back that up.

deals.headline: Beauty buys into football.
deals.summary: Official beauty partner through 2028. L'Oréal's first football sponsorship.

article.standfirst: L'Oréal just signed its first-ever football sponsorship, and chose Paris Saint-Germain to do it.
body: PSG have confirmed L'Oréal as the club's official beauty partner through 2028. It's the French cosmetics giant's first move into the sport, and it lands with one of the most heavily backed clubs in Europe.

Football's commercial ceiling keeps rising because categories with nothing to do with the pitch (beauty, fashion, lifestyle) want a piece of the audience and content machine big clubs now run. PSG's off-pitch program is built for exactly this kind of crossover.
A beauty major choosing football over tennis or F1, where cosmetics brands usually sit, says the audience around the men's game has gotten too big to ignore.
article.close: Expect more unlikely categories to follow L'Oréal into football before this cycle is out.

article.standfirst: MILO just became an official NBA partner.
body: Nestlé has signed a multi-year global marketing partnership with the NBA, covering 21 markets including Australia and New Zealand. MILO, Nescau and Nesquik all become Official Partners, with activations across Jr. NBA programs, NBA Global Games and NBA House starting from January 2027.

A brand this tied to junior cricket here is now putting the same weight behind basketball, and doing it across 21 countries in one partnership rather than market by market. That's rights holders bundling scale the way streaming platforms bundle territories.
It also says basketball has earned a seat at the table alongside the sports MILO has backed at grassroots level for decades.
article.close: Expect MILO to lean hard on that grassroots playbook once the Aussie and Kiwi activations land.

article.standfirst: JD Sports just signed its first-ever national rugby league partnership, and chose New Zealand Rugby League to do it.
body: JD becomes Major Partner and Official Sneaker Supplier to the Kiwis, Kiwi Ferns and Wheelchair Kiwis ahead of the Rugby League World Cup, with exclusive playing-day product and content tied to the tournament.

Sneaker brands have mostly chased football, basketball and the NBA/NFL orbit. A first national rugby league partnership says the category now sees real commercial upside in the code, with the World Cup's global stage probably doing the heavy lifting.
Expect other footwear brands to take notice.
article.close: Rugby league might be about to become footwear's next battleground.

deals.headline: Thirty years. Thirteen partnerships.
deals.summary: League-wide partnership running since 1995 replaced by 13 club partnerships: seven new, four renewals, two existing.

article.standfirst: Visa just ended thirty years of league-wide NFL sponsorship to bet on individual teams instead.
body: The blanket partnership, running since 1995, lapsed and wasn't renewed. Visa replaced it with 13 separate team partnerships: seven brand new, four long-term renewals and two already in place. The renewals cover the Buffalo Bills, New England Patriots, Pittsburgh Steelers and San Francisco 49ers, while the new signings include the Dallas Cowboys, Kansas City Chiefs and Philadelphia Eagles.

A league logo buys visibility everywhere and control nowhere. Thirteen team partnerships buy Visa a say in which markets get which activations, plus fan data a blanket partnership never handed over, and a clearer read on return in each market.
Other blue-chip league sponsors, from banking to airlines and insurance, will be asking the same question before their next renewal.
article.close: Thirty years as one NFL partnership just became thirteen. Worth watching who copies the model next.

article.standfirst: Bridgestone is walking back into top-flight motorsport, this time as both tyre supplier and title sponsor.
body: The Japanese giant has signed on as Formula E's sole tyre supplier from the 2026/27 season, taking title billing on four marquee rounds including Mexico City and Tokyo. The new tyres are built from 65% recycled and renewable material, launching alongside the championship's next-gen GEN4 car.

A legacy tyre brand betting big on electric racing says plenty about where motorsport sponsorship money is heading. Pairing the comeback with a real sustainability figure, rather than just a logo on the sidewall, gives Bridgestone a story to tell well beyond the partnership itself.
article.close: Expect more legacy automotive brands chasing the same electric-racing halo in seasons to come.

article.standfirst: Rice Stadium has stood for 76 years without a sponsor's name on it. Until now.
body: First Community Credit Union has signed a 20-year naming rights partnership, renaming the venue First Community Stadium and helping fund Rice University's $120 million Gateway Project renovation. It's the stadium's first-ever naming rights partnership, and it kicked in for Rice's home game against UTSA.

Credit unions buying into college sports isn't new, but tying the partnership directly to stadium financing is sharper. It turns sponsorship into a funding tool for schools without a billion-dollar athletics budget.
Expect more mid-major programs to chase this model instead of waiting on state money.
article.close: Naming rights used to be for the big programs. Not anymore.

article.standfirst: Bloom Energy just signed the second-biggest jersey patch partnership in NBA history, and this one's coming from the energy sector.
body: The Philadelphia 76ers have named the fuel-cell energy company their new patch partner, replacing Crypto.com, in a multi-year partnership that also covers the Delaware Blue Coats, with a seven-figure community investment attached. It lands as LeBron James's arrival spikes ticket and merchandise demand in Philadelphia.

Energy infrastructure money is chasing NBA real estate the way crypto and fintech did a few years back. Golden State carries IREN, and Philadelphia has now picked up the sector's second-biggest cheque. Basketball's reach is being priced at AI-boom rates, before AI itself has any real link to the sport.
article.close: Expect more energy and AI infrastructure names on NBA jerseys before the season's out.

deals.headline: Mascots get NIL partnerships.
deals.summary: First-of-its-kind mascot NIL partnership via Learfield. Touchdowns trigger shelter cat meals.

article.standfirst: Six college mascots have NIL partnerships now, and every touchdown their team scores earns a shelter cat a meal.
body: Friskies has signed what's being called a first-of-its-kind NIL partnership with six university mascots, including Truman the Tiger (Missouri), Aubie (Auburn) and Cosmo (BYU), brokered through Learfield. Scoring plays this season trigger donated meals for cats in shelters.
Mascots have sat on the fringe of the NIL boom since it opened beyond athletes, and this is the most creative use of it yet: a real in-game trigger instead of a logo on a costume.
It's cheap, carries almost no scandal risk, and gives brands a lane into college sports that doesn't compete with athletes for NIL money.
article.close: Expect more brands chasing mascots next, not quarterbacks.

deals.headline: Equity in her own tee.
deals.summary: First signature kicking tee in women's rugby, with 20% of every sale to de Goede.

article.standfirst: A New Zealand kicking-tee brand just gave a Canadian rugby captain equity in her own gear.
body: Rugby Bricks has signed World Player of the Year Sophie de Goede for the first signature kicking tee in women's rugby. The RB Vortex is co-designed by de Goede, with a red colourway for her Canadian heritage, and she takes 20% of every unit sold.

Signature product partnerships with revenue share are common in men's sport (boots, bats, rackets) but rare in women's rugby, where sponsorship infrastructure is still catching up. A boutique brand backing a genuine star with real upside, rather than chasing a marquee logo partnership, builds credibility fast.
article.close: More equipment brands will start trading flat fees for equity in the athletes wearing their gear.

deals.summary: Field naming rights worth up to US$22.8M, now Databricks Field.

article.standfirst: An AI infrastructure company just bought naming rights to a Power Four football stadium.
body: Databricks has locked in a partnership worth up to US$22.8M for naming rights to Cal's Memorial Stadium field, now Databricks Field, plus helmet branding through the 2026 season. It's a homecoming of sorts: the company was founded out of UC Berkeley.

College stadium naming rights used to be insurance companies and regional banks. Now it's AI infrastructure players with the deepest pockets in tech, buying brand equity with a young, technical audience and the alumni base that built them.
article.close: Expect more AI money to show up on stadiums before it shows up on jerseys.

deals.headline: La Liga partnerships itself in.
deals.summary: Exclusive global licence for real-money La Liga games outside Spain.

article.standfirst: La Liga has just become a real-money gambling operator.
body: Spain's top football league has signed an exclusive global licensing partnership with B2B studio LIGAS Gaming, letting it build and distribute real-money football games under the La Liga brand across regulated markets outside Spain.

That's a real shift in how a league makes money from gambling. Rather than collecting ad dollars from a betting sponsor, La Liga now earns directly off every wager placed inside its own branded product.
With betting-ad rules tightening across multiple markets, licensing the IP directly lets a rights holder keep the upside while sidestepping some of that scrutiny.
article.close: Expect more leagues to start treating real-money gaming as a product they own outright, not just an ad category they sell into.

deals.headline: A sub shop buys a trophy.

article.standfirst: A US sandwich chain just bought naming rights to an English football trophy.
body: Jersey Mike's is the new title sponsor of the EFL Trophy, now renamed the Jersey Mike's Trophy, in a five-year partnership worth around £5 million, the most lucrative commercial partnership in the competition's history. It covers League One, League Two and invited academy sides, and lands alongside Jersey Mike's push into the UK and Ireland, where it's targeting up to 400 new stores.
Going in through a lower-tier cup rather than a Premier League shirt is a cheaper way to buy visibility while a brand is still opening stores, long before it needs top-flight prices to get noticed.
article.close: Expect more US challenger brands to use the undercard to get a foothold in English football before they ever go near the main event.

deals.headline: Mbappé takes equity.
deals.summary: Leaves Nike after 20 years, taking equity instead of a standard fee.

article.standfirst: Kylian Mbappé just walked away from Nike after 20 years, and picked equity over a bigger cheque.
body: He's signed with Swiss brand On, taking equity in the business instead of a standard endorsement fee. On will build its first football boots in 2027, and has already added Thierry Henry as director of football.

The equity angle matters more than the boots. On is betting that owning part of a challenger brand beats another decade of royalty cheques from the market leader, and Mbappé's happy to bet alongside them. Federer proved the model works in tennis, and On is running the same play in football.
Expect more superstars to ask for equity over a signing bonus.
article.close: Boot partnerships used to be about who pays the most. Now the smart ones are about who owns the most.

deals.headline: Kitchen gear meets the pit lane.
deals.summary: Multi-year partnership across F1, IndyCar, Hypercar and F1 Academy, including R&D access.

article.standfirst: McLaren Racing just signed a kitchen appliance brand as an official partner, and the partnership goes well past logos on the car.
body: SharkNinja is now a multi-year partner across McLaren's Formula 1, Arrow McLaren IndyCar, Hypercar and F1 ACADEMY programmes. The partnership folds SharkNinja into the team's Racing Accelerator Programme, giving the appliance maker access to McLaren's engineering process for product development, not just trackside branding.

Motorsport sponsorship has traditionally sold speed and glamour. This one sells R&D access. When a consumer brand buys into a race team's engineering process rather than a grid slot, sponsorship starts looking more like a product partnership than a media buy, and that's a much harder asset for a rival to copy than a logo.
article.close: Expect more tech and consumer brands chasing access over airtime.

deals.headline: AI on the cricket shirt.
deals.summary: Five years with the Hobart Hurricanes and Tasmanian Tigers, $1M+ to grassroots.

article.standfirst: Firmus Technologies just put its name on Cricket Tasmania's playing shirts.
body: The Australian AI infrastructure company has signed a five-year partnership as principal partner of the Hobart Hurricanes and major partner of the Tasmanian Tigers, across both BBL and WBBL. Over $1 million of it goes straight into grassroots cricket through a new program called Beyond Boundaries.

AI and data infrastructure firms are cashed up right now, but most of that spend goes on compute rather than brand building. Front-of-shirt space on a regional cricket team is a fast way to buy mainstream trust outside the tech press, and tying it to grassroots funding makes the partnership harder to dismiss as a vanity buy.
article.close: More AI infrastructure names on sporting shirts feels inevitable from here.

deals.summary: Kit partnership to 2033, reported at €120M, plus naming rights to the Seixal academy.

article.standfirst: adidas just bought naming rights to the academy that produced Bernardo Silva, João Félix and Rúben Dias.
body: adidas has extended its kit partnership with Benfica through 2033, reported at €120 million and the biggest sponsorship in Portuguese football history. It stretches a relationship that goes back to 1997, and the new terms hand adidas naming rights to Benfica's Seixal training academy, which becomes the adidas Benfica Campus.

Kit partnerships usually buy visibility on match day. This one buys adidas a permanent presence inside the pipeline that actually produces the players, turning a facility into brand real estate instead of just matchday exposure.
Once every major stadium already has a naming partner, training grounds look like the next thing clubs can sell.
article.close: Sponsorship money is starting to chase where players are made, not just where they're worn.

deals.headline: Crypto casino on the sleeve.
deals.summary: Unlicensed crypto casino lands Sunderland's sleeve sponsorship.

article.standfirst: Sunderland just became the 11th Premier League club this season to sign a shirt sponsor that isn't licensed to operate in the UK.
body: Sunderland have signed Shuffle, a crypto casino platform licensed only in Curaçao, as sleeve sponsor across the Premier League, domestic cups and the UEFA Europa League. The multi-year partnership replaces previous sponsor Serios Group and debuted on the shirt against Arsenal.

Front-of-shirt gambling ads are now banned in the Premier League, and sleeves have become the workaround. Unlicensed operators are filling that gap faster than regulators can close it, with a government consultation on banning them unlikely to bite before 2027/28. Entain has been writing to rival clubs urging them to cut ties, yet eleven clubs now carry unlicensed brands anyway.
article.close: The front of the shirt is regulated. The sleeve, for now, isn't.

deals.headline: Record shirt. Record partnership.
deals.summary: Record shirt sponsorship for Liverpool.

article.standfirst: Liverpool just ended a 17-year sponsorship to sign one that pays more than double.
body: Liverpool have named Turkish Airlines as their new front-of-shirt sponsor from 2027, replacing Standard Chartered after 17 years. The five-year partnership is reported at roughly £60 million a year, close to £300 million in total and the biggest shirt sponsorship in football history.

Standard Chartered's partnership was one of the longest-running in the Premier League. Walking away from that kind of continuity for this kind of number shows how far shirt values have moved. Airlines have circled football's biggest shirts for years (Emirates, Qatar Airways), and Turkish Airlines just set a new price for the privilege.
article.close: Expect the next round of Premier League shirt renewals to be priced off this partnership, not the one it replaced.

deals.headline: Starbucks goes front of shirt.
deals.summary: Starbucks' first football shirt deal, as Toulouse's sleeve sponsor for 2026/27.

article.standfirst: Starbucks just put its name on a football shirt for the first time anywhere in the world.
body: The coffee giant has signed as an official partner of Ligue 1 side Toulouse FC. It's Starbucks' first-ever club shirt sponsorship in football, after years of stadium and event tie-ins but never a jersey.

Going with a mid-table Ligue 1 club rather than a Premier League giant looks like a deliberate test run. Toulouse gets a genuinely global brand on the shirt, and Starbucks gets to trial football sponsorship at a fraction of the cost of a top-league partnership.
article.close: Watch for Starbucks to move up market fast if the Toulouse partnership lands well.

article.standfirst: Kin Insurance just put its logo on every jersey across Florida State's athletic department: all 18 sports, one partnership.
body: The insurer becomes the first brand ever to appear as a jersey patch across FSU's full sporting program, in a four-year agreement that also makes it the school's preferred insurance partner. It debuted on the football jersey against SMU.

Most jersey-patch partnerships stay locked to the marquee sport, where the cameras are. Buying across an entire athletic department trades spotlight exposure for blanket presence: every roster, and every recruiting pitch the school makes.
article.close: Expect more brands to buy the whole department instead of just the biggest sport.

deals.headline: Surfing gets its streamer.

article.standfirst: Kayo just bought the broadcast rights to a surfing league that doesn't launch until 2028.
body: Kayo Sports and BINGE have locked in exclusive rights to the new Surfing Super League, a franchise-based comp built on a fixed, LIV Golf-style format: eight weeks, set weekend timeslots and 50 hours of coverage. The partnership was signed 17 months before a single heat gets surfed.

This is a format bet. Kayo is backing a made-for-TV competition more than a year out from its first heat, with no existing tour or star roster to lean on yet. Surf has always fought its broadcast window, and a fixed format designed for TV from day one might be the fix the traditional tour never found.
article.close: Expect more sports to build the broadcast partnership first and the competition second.
